en.html:
Young. Apparently beautiful also.

Nothing suspicious in that. In this royal castle, women satisfying those two conditions would hardly be rare.

Choosing this steep path was a little unusual for a woman, perhaps, but again, not enough for suspicion. Ichijou was managing it without any difficulty.

Yet this woman had caught my attention.

Nothing outlandish about her clothes. They were very plain, but not the practical plainness of an official's clothes, like Ms. Iwata's. Nor was she dressed as a servant doing odd jobs.

Perhaps that was it.

Clothing was supposed to announce a person's rank and position. Hers had declined to make the announcement.

There was refinement in her face. Looking at that alone, one might take her for a daughter of some great house. Include the clothes, and the conclusion no longer fitted. Not a court lady serving in the inner quarters, not a priestess at the castle shrine. Not a clerk, a soldier, a cleaner, or a cook from the dining hall.

Every rank and every duty was strictly assigned in this little society. Everybody had a place, and in none of those places could I put her.

She stood apart. Her appearance, and that air of not knowing where to be—both.

en.html:
One lost woman met two guides. A chemical reaction occurred. The product was three lost people.

The rescuers also required rescuing now.

Raasta hum dikhaayenge. We will show the way. Such was the promise. We had indeed shown her a great deal of way. This way, that way, several other ways whose contribution to the destination remained doubtful. Only the correct way had been modest enough not to present itself.

In ordinary arithmetic, add two people to one and three result. In our case, the addition had also multiplied the original problem. Nobody had known this was a possible branch of mathematics. The three of us were exploring it on foot.

By the time we noticed, the sky had turned red. The crows were calling, and each call was hurting the ear.

en.html:
The princess of the Okabe house said it without emotion.

For a while I had no words to put after hers. Ichijou also had fallen silent.

The stick had dropped at her feet. Out of all possible directions, it had chosen west, where the cliff was. I quietly kicked it away and began fitting the pieces together in my mind.

...So that was why she did not fit here.

Yoritsuna Okabe. Once, his power had rivaled Moriuji Ashikaga's. He had even held the office of Director of the Board of Censors, a post normally reserved for the imperial family.

His daughter.

A great name she had been born into, but acknowledgment of that greatness was no longer permitted. Noble birth remained; wealth and status had gone. And among the common people, there was no place for her either.

As she had said, the daughter of a defeated general. Nothing else was left for her to be.

In this castle, how could she not stand out?

Sakurako"I see... Then it must be very trying for you."
Sakurako"For me also... though my difficulties are nothing compared with yours, since you both have work to do. Still, in an unfamiliar place, so many things..."

This was not particular to Fudaraku. Fortress roads were often more complicated than ordinary travel required. Once an enemy had broken through the gates, delay him wherever possible and split up his forces—that was the purpose.

en.html:
Two people whose direction sense was in a very serious condition had found complete agreement.

Neither could find the way, so naturally the world must be rebuilt. Dig underneath it. Put another world on top. Still lost? Add a bridge, bhai. We have not yet exhausted the sky. The sun may have to move a little, but surely it will understand the inconvenience of a turning.

I alone had been left behind. We had not found our destination, and already I was losing the argument about how to demolish the journey.
